Odile Marchetti said on October 9, in the greenhouse sensor rollout discussion: "We install humidity sensors in all four greenhouse bays before the first frost. Bay two gets the pilot unit first, because it lost the most seedlings last winter." Pell Vasquez answered "Agreed." and then added: "The sensors report every fifteen minutes; anything slower misses the overnight drop."

The work now stands like this: sensors go into all four greenhouse bays before the first frost, and bay two goes first as the pilot unit, because it lost the most seedlings last winter. The fifteen-minute reporting interval is part of the same plan, not a separate question. The two of them have settled the plan rather than floated it, and the reason for the interval is stated outright.

My read is that bay two is now the test bench for the whole rollout, so whatever the pilot shows about overnight humidity decides how the other three bays are set up. That suggests to me that the fifteen-minute interval is no longer open for the other bays either. If the pilot catches the overnight drop at that cadence, I read that as the evidence for putting the same interval in the other bays without arguing it again before the install.

Where does it end? Does the fifteen-minute interval hold for the other three bays too? Is the first frost date firm enough to plan the install order around?
